overview: Rise 5.99's AutoHead is a health-gated head eater with the same two-tick structure as the sibling AutoSoup: select the head hotbar slot with C09, use it with C08, then on the following tick send the C07 release and the C09 switch back. The gate is ticksExisted greater than 10 and getHealth() below the Health setting (default 15), and the cycle repeats on a randomized delay between Min Delay and Max Delay (defaults 300-500ms). Slot selection uses PlayerUtil.findHead(), which matches any hotbar stack whose display name contains 'Head' with no ItemFood requirement, so golden heads, player heads and decorative skulls all qualify. There are no window clicks anywhere and no drop step: the entire mechanism is C09/C08/C07 slot traffic against the player's own hotbar.

sections.p: The eat is split across two pre-motion events, mirroring AutoSoup exactly minus the drop. The first tick, gated on ticksExisted > 10 and health below the threshold, locates a head with PlayerUtil.findHead(), converts the container slot to a hotbar index (findHead() - 36, with -37 as the not-found sentinel), and sends C09PacketHeldItemChange(head) followed by C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement with the head stack, arming the switchBack flag. The next tick's switchBack branch sends C07PacketPlayerDigging RELEASE_USE_ITEM at BlockPos.ORIGIN facing down, then C09 back to the player's real held slot, and clears the flag. The release and slot restore are always one full tick after the use, never in the same tick.

The cycle is clocked by a TimeUtil and a decidedTimer millisecond value. When the gate opens, the module computes delayFirst as floor of the lower bound and delaySecond as ceil of the upper bound, then picks RandomUtils.nextInt(delayFirst, delaySecond) and resets the timer, so the default 300-500ms settings yield roughly 2-3 eat cycles per second while health stays low. If findHead() returns -1, head stays at the -37 sentinel and the C09/C08 pair is skipped, but the delay is still re-rolled, so an empty hotbar does not accelerate the loop. The ticksExisted > 10 guard suppresses eating during the first half-second after spawn or respawn.

Each successful cycle emits, across two ticks: C09(head), C08(use with the head stack), then C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM and C09(real slot). No C0E window clicks are ever sent, and there is no drop packet - the eaten head leaves no bowl, so the module is one packet lighter than AutoSoup. The C08 payload is the itemstack constructor (use on air), and the C07 uses BlockPos.ORIGIN with EnumFacing.DOWN. The release arriving one tick after the use is the module's defining timing property, identical to AutoSoup's.

files.label: AutoHead.java
files.explanation: The module is one pre-motion handler with two phases, structurally identical to Rise's AutoSoup minus the drop-bowl option. The switchBack branch (lines 38-43) sends the C07 release and the C09 slot restore one tick after the use, clears the flag and returns. The gate (lines 45-61) only runs when the flag is clear: ticksExisted > 10, health below the threshold, findHead() - 36 into the hotbar index, the C09 + C08 pair, and the delay re-roll with RandomUtils.nextInt over floor(min) to ceil(max) followed by timer.reset().\n\nThe -37 sentinel distinguishes 'no head found' from a nonexistent hotbar slot. There is no drop: heads do not leave a bowl, so the cycle ends at the release and slot restore, one packet fewer than AutoSoup's. onDisable clears both switchBack and the sentinel so a mid-cycle disable cannot leave the slot stuck on the head. The module never opens a window and never sends C0E; its entire interaction surface is C09/C08/C07 hotbar traffic.

files.label: PlayerUtil.java (findHead slot finder)
files.explanation: findHead (lines 337-347) scans container slots 36 to 44, the hotbar in the player inventory container, and returns the first stack that is non-null, has stackSize above 0, and whose display name contains 'Head'. Notably it omits the ItemFood check that findGap and findSoup apply, so any item named 'Head' qualifies: golden heads, player heads, zombie skulls and decorative heads alike. The display-name predicate is the only filter.\n\nThe return value is a container index, so the module subtracts 36 to obtain the hotbar index used in the C09 and the inventory.getStackInSlot(head) lookup for the C08 payload. Only the hotbar is scanned, so the module depends on the player pre-loading heads into the hotbar. The same class provides findSoup and findGap for the sibling AutoSoup and AutoGap modules with the identical slots-36-to-44 scan pattern and stricter food predicates.

countering.label: FastConsume (consume duration)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's FastConsume stamps InventoryData.consumeTime on a RIGHT_CLICK_AIR or RIGHT_CLICK_BLOCK interaction with an edible item and flags a PlayerItemConsumeEvent that arrives within consume-time (default 1280ms) of the stamp, raising 'consume time less than allowed.' Golden heads are edible items, so the use arms the timer.\n\nRise's cycle sends C08 (use) and the C07 release one tick later, roughly 50ms apart, so on any server where head consumption completes at release the PlayerItemConsumeEvent lands about 50ms after the stamp, far under the 1280ms floor, and the check fires on every eat. On vanilla servers the one-tick release is too early for the 32-tick use window, no consume event fires, and the check stays silent. The split is the same honest one as AutoSoup: FastConsume bites exactly on the instant-consumption servers the module is written for.

countering.label: ItemSwitchSpeed (switch after use)
countering.explanation: Hawk's ItemSwitchSpeed marks a player as having used something on InteractItemEvent or InteractWorldEvent, then checks the next ItemSwitchEvent against the stored lastSwitchTick, punishing when the gap is under minSwitchTicks (default 1) and always consuming the usedSomething entry.\n\nRise's cycle sends C09(head) and the C08 use in the same tick, then the switch-back C09 one tick later, so the switch-back's delta is exactly 1 tick and the check rewards it at the default minimum of 1. Like AutoSoup, the module deliberately delays the slot restore by a full tick, and that one-tick margin is what keeps it under the default gate; raising minSwitchTicks to 2 makes every cycle flag. The absence of a drop packet does not change the math - the check only measures switches, and there is exactly one switch-back per cycle.

countering.label: FastClick (window click rate, missed)
countering.explanation: NoCheatPlus FastClick counts C0E inventory clicks into an ActionFrequency with five 200ms buckets, comparing the newest bucket against the short-term limit of 4 and the one-second window against the normal limit of 15, with lag division via TickTask. Only real window clicks feed the ledger.\n\nAutoHead never sends a C0E packet: slot selection is C09 held-item changes and the use is C08, so FastClick's ledger never increments regardless of eat rate. The check that exists to stop autosteal-style click spam is structurally blind to a C09/C08/C07 implementation, exactly as with the sibling AutoSoup and AutoGap modules. NCP's inventory countering for this module therefore falls entirely on the Open check and the use-item adapters rather than the click-rate path.
